subject: chemistry
question_text: Explain oxidation and reduction in terms of (a) oxygen, (b) hydrogen and (c) electron transfer, with one example each.

verification.note: PREDICTED, not asked. This card comes from the enumeration sweep of Chapter 5 (Stoichiometry): the Fastrack chemistry section (book pp.66-72) asks the redox-reaction definition (VSAQ 16) but never the classical oxygen, hydrogen and electron-transfer definitions of oxidation and reduction, which the syllabus develops before the oxidation-number concept. Only ONE source book is held for chemistry, so the two-book union check is PENDING. This chapter has NO Long Answer section in the book, so no 8-mark form is invented. The 2+1+1 mark split is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. AI chemistry check 2026-08-25. Replaced the metaphor 'one survivor' in the s3 memory tip with plain wording (Rule 41). No marked line changed.

steps.label: Oxygen and hydrogen senses
lines: Oxidation is the addition of oxygen:
Reduction is the removal of oxygen:
CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O (CuO is reduced).
Oxidation is the removal of hydrogen:
Reduction is the addition of hydrogen:
in the same reaction Cl₂ gains hydrogen,
steps.why: The classical definitions describe redox by what is visibly gained or lost — oxygen or hydrogen — and each definition needs its own example equation to earn its mark.
common_mistakes: Swapping the hydrogen sense: LOSING hydrogen is oxidation.
Giving definitions with no example equations.
Labelling the wrong species — in CuO + H₂, the CuO is reduced while H₂ is oxidised.
steps.memory_tip: Oxygen and hydrogen run opposite ways: gaining oxygen is oxidation, gaining hydrogen is reduction.
steps.margin_note: Four short definitions, each with a labelled example — one mark per sense.

steps.label: Electron-transfer sense
lines: Oxidation is the LOSS of electrons:
Reduction is the GAIN of electrons:
steps.why: The electron definition is the modern, general one: it covers reactions where no oxygen or hydrogen appears at all, and it is the basis of the ion-electron balancing method.
common_mistakes: Writing the half equations without the electrons shown.
steps.memory_tip: OIL RIG — Oxidation Is Loss, Reduction Is Gain (of electrons).
steps.margin_note: The two half equations with visible electrons earn this mark.

steps.label: The summary

lines.text: Oxidation = loss of electrons ; Reduction = gain of electrons

lines: The electron definition includes the oxygen
and hydrogen definitions as special cases,
so it is the definition used for all redox
steps.why: Closing with the electron definition states which of the three senses is general — that judgment is what makes the answer more than three disconnected definitions.
common_mistakes: Ending without saying the electron sense is the general one.
steps.memory_tip: Three senses, one general definition: the electron definition covers every case.
steps.margin_note: Box the electron-sense pair; the closing sentence completes the answer.

insider_note: Four marks over three senses, so they are not weighted equally: oxygen and hydrogen share two, the electron sense has one, and the closing judgment that the electron sense is the general one is the fourth. That last sentence is the cheapest mark here.
